title: Self-driving laboratory optimizes organic hole-transport thin films
summary: A robotic laboratory used model-based optimization to select thin-film compositions and processing conditions, execute experiments and learn from their measured optical and electronic properties. The reported demonstration optimized hole mobility in organic hole-transport materials used in perovskite solar cells and electronics. This description is limited to the paper abstract; it does not assert a numerical mobility gain.
ai_technology: Closed-loop self-driving laboratory with autonomous optimization
organization: University of British Columbia; Harvard University; University of Toronto

evidence.tested: Closed-loop composition and processing experiments on organic hole-transport thin films, with measured hole mobility as an optimization target.
evidence.unknown: Abstract and publication metadata reviewed; detailed optimization history, baseline comparisons and durability were not assessed.
evidence.ai_role: A model-based optimizer selected subsequent experiments using measurements from the robotic platform.
